articles.title: Vikings Wanted Kirk Cousins Trade Before Wentz Struggled, Latest NFL Rumors on Raiders Talks
articles.summary: Despite the conventional wisdom being the Minnesota Vikings pursued the Kirk Cousins trade in direct response to Carson Wentz's performance on Monday Night Football, they actually reached out to the Las Vegas Raiders before their 23-6 loss to the Buffalo Bills.
articles.body:
Despite the conventional wisdom being the Minnesota Vikings pursued the Kirk Cousins trade in direct response to Carson Wentz's performance on Monday Night Football, they actually reached out to the Las Vegas Raiders before their 23-6 loss to the Buffalo Bills.

Per ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport , the Vikings' first call to the Raiders about Cousins came a few hours before Monday's kickoff and they "made it clear" they wanted to see how Wentz played before taking things further.

The report also noted Minnesota's initial offer of a fifth-round pick for Cousins was of no interest to the Raiders, but the tide shifted when it was bumped up to a 2027 third-round selection:

Kirk Trade Result of Vikings' 'Desperation'

"It was not a deal the Raiders wanted, nor were looking to make, especially when Minnesota's initial offer was a fifth-round draft pick, according to sources.

"But once the Vikings upped their offer to a third-round pick, the Raiders had discussions about whether the trade made sense, and here's where they landed:

"Not only would they be receiving a third-round pick, but they also would be freeing up $10 million in cash for the 2027 season, as the bonus guarantee owed to Cousins would shift to Minnesota's responsibility. It was not a trade that the Raiders enjoyed making, but it was one they believed would be in the best interests of the organization."

Wentz got the start against Buffalo with Kyler Murray unavailable due to a hamstring injury. He played well when called upon earlier in the season, including throwing for 133 yard and three touchdowns in a 39-22 win over the Green Bay Packers in Week 1.

Things did not go well this time around for Wentz. He finished 8-of-25 for 81 yards with two interceptions against Buffalo's defense.

The Vikings got the deal done with the Raiders shortly before Tuesday's 4 p.m. ET trade deadline by giving up their 2027 third-round seelction.

Even before Wentz's disastrous outing and Murray's injury, there were reasons for the Vikings to explore the quarterback trade market. Murray ranks 26th in QBR and 27th in success rate out of 31 qualified quarterbacks this season.

Cousins has been much better than expected in nine starts with the Raiders. He has thrown for 2,430 yards, 20 touchdowns and completed 64.1 percent of his attempts.

Murray, Wentz and Max Brosmer combined have thrown for 1,286 yards, eight touchdowns, five interceptions and completed 60.9 percent of their attempts.

Adding to the value for Minnesota is Cousins' built-in familiarity with head coach Kevin O'Connell's system from their two seasons together in 2022 and '23. He was also the Vikings quarterback for Justin Jefferson's first four seasons.

Jefferson averaged 98 receptions, 1,475 yards and 7.5 touchdowns per season from 2020 to '23. His numbers have dipped to 73 receptions, 991 yards and 5.3 touchdowns per season without Cousins.

Minnesota's defense has been the best in the NFL this season with 14.6 points allowed per game, so any upgrade at quarterback would have made this team a top-tier Super Bowl contender.

Cousins is more than capable of playing well for the offense to succeed, especially knowing the Vikings defense will more than hold up their end of the bargain.

articles.title: $105 million Pro Bowler could be the missing piece the Cincinnati Bengals need to make a serious playoff push
articles.summary: The Cincinnati Bengals missed an important opportunity to strengthen their secondary before the NFL trade deadline.
articles.body: The Cincinnati Bengals missed an important opportunity to strengthen their secondary before the NFL trade deadline. Their failed attempt to add cornerback help has left a familiar weakness unresolved, and there is still a veteran option available. Four-time Pro Bowler Marshon Lattimore remains without a team after his release from Washington. With Cincinnati preparing for a crucial stretch of the season, bringing in the former New Orleans Saints star could give its defense some much-needed experience and depth. The move would carry some risk, but the potential reward is worth considering.Cincinnati Bengals could find a defensive solution in Marshon LattimoreCincinnati's need for another cornerback has become increasingly difficult to overlook. The Bengals have DJ Turner as a reliable option on the outside, while Dax Hill offers flexibility as both a slot and outside defender. The problem begins when the coaching staff tries to use both players in their preferred roles.If Hill moves inside, the Bengals need another dependable outside corner. If he stays outside, the slot position becomes less settled. Jalen Davis, Josh Newton and DJ Ivey have all been involved in the rotation, but none has provided the consistency Cincinnati needs.That is where Lattimore enters the discussion.Bleacher Report's Moe Moton recently identified Cincinnati and Detroit as two suitable destinations for the veteran cornerback. Moton pointed out that neither team managed to land a cornerback before the deadline.“Some speculated that the Cincinnati Bengals and Detroit Lions would try to trade for cornerbacks before the deadline,” wrote Moton. “Neither team acquired one. Lattimore could be a solid in-season acquisition for either club.”Lattimore has earned nearly $105 million during his 10-year NFL career. He was selected 11th overall by New Orleans in 2017 and won Defensive Rookie of the Year honors. Four Pro Bowl selections followed, establishing him as one of the more respected cornerbacks of his generation.Lattimore's injury history makes the move a calculated riskThere is a reason Lattimore remains available, though. His recent seasons have been interrupted by injuries, and his performances have not always matched the level he showed during his best years in New Orleans.He started seven games in 2022, 10 in 2023 and nine in 2024 before moving to Washington. His time with the Commanders also failed to bring much stability. He appeared in only two games during the 2024 season and nine in 2025 before Washington released him in March 2026. He also suffered an ACL injury in Week 9 of 2025, making his recovery an important factor for any interested team.Cincinnati would need to assess his fitness before making a commitment. Still, the Bengals do not necessarily need Lattimore to return to his Pro Bowl level immediately. A healthy veteran who can handle meaningful snaps would already give the coaching staff more choices.The timing matters, too. Cincinnati faces Pittsburgh in Week 11, a matchup with major AFC North implications. The Bengals have made their intentions clear with an aggressive roster approach this season, but their secondary remains an area that needs attention.Lattimore may not be the complete answer. Yet leaving a clear weakness untouched could prove more costly when the games become more important. For Cincinnati, this is a chance to add experience without giving up another draft pick.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: NFL reassigns 3 officials following nationwide FAA ground stop
articles.summary: The ground stop order was lifted Friday night, but not before it affected games in the NFL and college football this weekend.
articles.body:
The ground stop order issued by the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) on Friday has now affected the NFL after having an impact on this weekend's college football games .

On Saturday morning, the NFL announced that several officiating assignments for Week 10 have been adjusted. Officials were reassigned to games that are within driving distance of their hometowns.

Barry Anderson and Duane Heydt, who normally serve as umpires, along with side judge Don Willard, will take on referee duties on Sunday.

Anderson will officiate the Jacksonville Jaguars-Tennessee Titans game in Tennessee; Heydt has been assigned to work the Carolina Panthers-New Orleans Saints game in New Orleans; and Willard will have double-duty first refereeing the Miami Dolphins-Indianapolis Colts game in Indianapolis at 1 p.m. ET before making the trip to Cincinnati for Sunday night's game between the Bengals and Pittsburgh Steelers at 8:20 p.m. ET.

"Each of the league's 17 officiating crews have a backup referee identified, and that individual trains throughout the year to work at the referee position should the need arise," the NFL said.

According to The Ringer's Tom Pelissero , another change will see replay duties in the Panthers-Saints game handled by the league's replay center in New York and not an official in the stadium.

The ground stop order was put in place on Friday due to a "temporary telecommunications outage" affecting air traffic control, the FAA announced .

That stop was lifted as of 8:15 p.m. ET Friday, but even with flights allowed to resume, it led to kickoff changes for some college games. Almost all of the Power Four conferences have teams that were prevented from reaching their destinations. Only the ACC has every team already ready to go. One SEC matchup — Ole Miss vs. Oklahoma — was postponed to Sunday .

"It'll be slow," Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy said Friday about the resumption of nationwide air travel.

It's the second nationwide ground stop since 9/11, per ABC News , which noted that this last happened in 2023 . At the time, pilots were unable to access their pre-departure paperwork because the FAA NOTAM (Notice To all Air Missions) system — used to disseminate flight hazards and real-time restrictions to pilots — went down.

articles.title: Mac Jones Trade Demand from 49ers to Vikings Revealed in New NFL Rumors After Kirk Cousins Deal
articles.summary: The San Francisco 49ers' high asking price reportedly ended the Minnesota Vikings' pursuit of quarterback Mac Jones ahead of the NFL trade deadline this week.
articles.body:
The San Francisco 49ers' high asking price reportedly ended the Minnesota Vikings' pursuit of quarterback Mac Jones ahead of the NFL trade deadline this week.

According to ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport , the Vikings called the Niners about Jones, but discussions ended when San Francisco asked for a second-round pick and more in exchange for its backup signal-caller.

Instead, the Vikings opted to bring Kirk Cousins back to Minnesota, acquiring him from the Las Vegas Raiders for a third-round pick.

Kirk Trade Result of Vikings' 'Desperation'

Per Schefter and Rapoport, the pre-deadline conversations were not the first time the Vikings and 49ers held talks focused on Jones.

However, 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan reportedly views Jones as a "franchise-caliber quarterback," and the Niners did not want to trade him unless they got an offer that they "had no choice but to accept."

Jones, 28, is in the midst of his second season with the 49ers after stints as a member of the New England Patriots and Jacksonville Jaguars.

While he has not attempted a pass this season due to starting quarterback Brock Purdy staying healthy, Jones played a significant role in San Francisco reaching the playoffs last season.

Jones appeared in 11 games and made eight starts, as Purdy struggled through multiple injuries.

The one-time Pro Bowler went 5-3 in those starts, completing 69.6 percent of his passes for 2,151 yards, 13 touchdowns and six interceptions.

Originally selected 15th overall by the Patriots in the 2021 NFL draft, he did not pan out as a starter in New England, but there is seemingly a strong chance that Jones could get a chance to start somewhere next season provided he opts to leave San Francisco in free agency.

Should that happen, Jones would be following a path similar to Sam Darnold, who spent 2023 as the 49ers' backup before earning Pro Bowl honors with the Vikings in 2024 and leading the Seattle Seahawks to a Super Bowl win in 2025.

With Cousins, Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz all playing on expiring contracts, Jones could very well be an option for Minnesota in free agency this coming offseason.

For now, the Vikings are hoping Cousins' return will breathe new life into an offense that has lagged well behind a defense that ranks first in the NFL in points allowed and second in yards allowed.

At 6-2, Minnesota is just a half-game behind the Chicago Bears for the NFC North lead, and with an improved offense, the Vikings could be Super Bowl contenders.

articles.title: Jets Icon Darrelle Revis Talks Aaron Glenn, Arch Manning, Coaching Interest & More in B/R Interview
articles.summary: As arguably the greatest player in New York Jets franchise history, Hall of Fame cornerback Darrelle Revis has lived through the team's thrilling highs and agonizing heartbreaks.
articles.body:
As arguably the greatest player in New York Jets franchise history, Hall of Fame cornerback Darrelle Revis has lived through the team's thrilling highs and agonizing heartbreaks.

So even with the Jets' 2-7 record entering Sunday's game against the 7-1 Buffalo Bills, Revis can still find reasons for optimism. While highlighting New York's three first-round picks in the 2027 NFL draft, the 41-year-old gave his thoughts on the future of head coach Aaron Glenn, who is 5-21 two years into the job.

"I think it's premature to fire Aaron Glenn. I just think it is," Revis told Bleacher Report. "I think with what we have in the value of the draft picks, I think we need to give him a third year to really hone in… The QB position always solves some of the issues when you got a great quarterback."

The 2027 draft class is expected to be loaded with talented signal-callers, giving the Jets a chance to finally secure their franchise quarterback after years of instability at the position. With prospects such as Oklahoma State's Drew Mestemaker and Notre Dame's CJ Carr rising up draft boards, Revis weighed in on who he'd like to see under center for New York, as well as what the team should do with its other first-round picks.

"If it's Arch Manning, we love it. He has so much potential," Revis said of the Texas quarterback. "And he comes from a family legacy that knows how to play at a high level of football. So, it's a lot of excitement ahead, I think."

He later added: "I like Leonard Moore, the cornerback from Notre Dame, he's a pretty solid cover corner. We need that back in the secondary, too. Seems like he'll bring a lot of leadership early on, with how he plays at Notre Dame. Coach [Marcus] Freeman is doing a great job developing those young men at Notre Dame."

A shutdown cornerback would surely solve New York's interception problem, as the team has just one pick in 26 games under Glenn. Revis is responsible for one of the greatest cornerback seasons in NFL history, setting a league record with 31 passes defended in 2009, so he knows what it takes to create a successful secondary. The seven-time Pro Bowler gave a thoughtful answer on what the Jets should do to improve their defensive backfield.

"When I played, for me, I've always tried to focus on great study habits. That's one. Attention to detail, especially in the back end of the secondary, only because it's such an uncomfortable position to play. The cornerback position and the safety position. If the ball goes over our head and it's a touchdown, it's an embarrassment," he said. "The fans are going wild about it. So we have to be very focused and have attention to detail in what we're doing and what we're trying to execute as a unit.

"There's a lot of communication on the back end amongst the safeties and the corners to make sure we're on the same page, to play at a very high level, and be playmakers. I think it's about being playmakers and making plays," he continued. "Our job is, we're the last line of defense, and our job is to stop people from making touchdowns. And I think that's the gist of it. And then also playmakers, just make plays in the passing game. If you can get your hands on that ball, we want to turn it over."

With so much insight and expertise, Revis has what it takes to be a successful defensive backs coach in the NFL. While he said he's satisfied with his current life in real estate business ventures and other investments, he clearly has a passion for teaching the tidbits that made him so successful in the league, and he revealed whether he would be willing to lend a hand to his old franchise.

"I'm here, I can be available. It has to be the right situation, obviously. But I'm here," Revis said when asked if he would be interested in a job as a DB coach. "The Jets, if they want to call and have a conversation, I'm open for it because it's for the betterment of the team and to improve the team and be a part of that new success that I believe is about to happen as well."

Whether or not he gets the call to join the team's coaching staff, Revis still makes his presence felt around the Jets. He recently attended New York's Nov. 1 game against the Las Vegas Raiders, partnering with American Express for the 2026 Shop Small activation at MetLife Stadium. The event spotlighted several local NYC-area small businesses as part of a tailgate pop-up, allowing fans to discover their unique offerings and engage with the business owners directly ahead of Small Business Saturday on Nov. 28.

"It's great to team up with Amex, they do a lot in the community for their clients. I think it was great, I was excited to be back in the area to support the team. ... I think small businesses are very vital and important to a local community," Revis said. "They bring people together. You build friendships, you build networks through those communities with small businesses. And I find it very exciting; that pop-up was very enlightening to see some of the creativity that some of these owners have with small businesses."

In Revis' eight seasons in New York, he experienced the success of back-to-back AFC Championship Game appearances in 2009 and 2010, as well as tough rebuild years that the current team is facing. As the Jets try to close out what will likely be a 16th straight year without a playoff appearance, Revis had advice for how Glenn and the players should approach the rest of this season.

"Aaron, as a player, he was a super competitor. I'm sure, as a coach, he is as well. I just would say to be optimistic," he said. "It's so tough to win on a Sunday, it really is. ... But I believe if you pay attention to the details of critiquing yourself as a head coach: What can I improve on? Where are my strengths? Where are my weaknesses? Where can I find a middle ground? And I think if he can do that on a week-to-week basis for the rest of the season, you can see more improvement in the team as well, because obviously he's the head coach, he's leading those guys. And maybe when you critique yourself that way, maybe you can get a couple more wins before the season is over, going into the offseason."

He added: "As a player, it can be frustrating for those guys, especially a guy like Garrett Wilson, whose track record is usually winning more games than losing. ... I know he wants to win now, and it can be frustrating that all the pieces are not falling into place. We paid him a ton of money, we have a lot of belief in his potential and his future. So, he will be a big part of our success in the near future as well. Once we can get a great quarterback in the draft, they can gel together and have that chemistry."

Despite the new incoming quarterback next year, Revis advocated for the Jets to hold on to veteran starter Geno Smith next season to ease the transition for the youngster.

"Love, love, love Geno as well. I think we need to bring Geno back. He's been playing well, even though the record doesn't show it, but his stats have been great. He doesn't turn over the ball a lot. He's a very smart quarterback. I think the new guy can come in and maybe sit, like [Fernando] Mendoza [with the Raiders]. Give the new quarterback some time to just get adjusted to the way of life of being a pro athlete," Revis said. "The players, I know it's frustrating, but show a lot of effort the rest of the games here in this season. Play hard, you're athletes, you know how to play the game. And see if you can squeeze in a couple wins going into the offseason, because that will rub off on you going into the new season."

As for the die-hard fans who stick with the Jets through all the highs and lows, Revis advised them to stay the course, pointing to the recent sports success in New York as a reason to be hopeful that brighter days are ahead for Gang Green.

"Man, I'll say this: the Knicks finally won. Obviously, it took 53 years. I think, right now, be patient. I know every week, we have such loyal fans. They wear the jerseys, they got man caves, they got it all. They come to support because they love the game and they want to win right now. I think that's great," he said. "I just think Darren Mougey, the GM, has done a great job with draft capital. I think we need to be excited for this upcoming draft, because there's no way that we're not going to pick a quarterback. We have to. There's so much college talent out there with these quarterbacks, and we should see who we pick.

"And I think whoever we pick, we should embrace it. We should embrace that. ... And we'll see. We'll just see. I'm very excited. And just be patient. I know this can be frustrating, but I think we should bring a lot of excitement into this new draft."

articles.title: Chiefs RB Kenneth Walker III ruled out for Week 10 matchup against Falcons with groin injury
articles.summary: Walker suffered the groin injury during Thursday's practice with the Chiefs.
articles.body:
Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Atlanta Falcons.

The NFL's second-leading rusher reported groin tightness on Friday morning and the team wants to "give him a week" to rest. Rookie running back Emmett Johnson will now handle first-team duties in Walker's absence.

Following Friday's practice, Chiefs head coach Andy Reid told reporters that the team wanted to see how Walker responded to treatment before making a final decision on his status for Week 10.

"We'll just see how he feels through this afternoon, with rehab and through tomorrow," Reid said. "Somewhere he tweaked it. We're kind of feeling it out just to see where we're at with that [groin]. We're not going to put him at risk. If he can go, he can go. If he can't, he can't."

Walker was listed as questionable on Friday's injury report .

In his first season with the Chiefs after signing a three-year, $43.05 million contract in March, Walker has 872 rushing yards and seven touchdowns through eight games. He is currently eight yards behind the NFL leader Bijan Robinson of the Falcons.

Johnson, the team's fifth-round pick in the 2026 draft out of Nebraska, has 111 rushing yards and a touchdown, plus 14 receptions for 237 and a touchdown this season. He has also served as the Chiefs' kick return man, picking up 318 return yards on 11 attempts.

Fantasy football impact of Walker's absence

Walker has not only helped carry the Chiefs offense but has also been one of fantasy football's best players over the season's first half. He has averaged 22.9 fantasy points per game in half-PPR scoring, second only to Jahmyr Gibbs among all running backs.

With Walker out, Johnson is a must-add in all fantasy leagues. At the time the news broke of Walker being ruled out, the rookie was available in 56% of Yahoo leagues. That number will skyrocket. Johnson has been one of the most valuable fantasy stashes all season for just such a situation. He has shown flashes in limited touches this season, including posting 22.8 fantasy points in Week 8 thanks to five receptions for 128 yards and a touchdown. He also found the end zone last week in a win over the Jets. Johnson will be a borderline fantasy RB1 in a matchup at Atlanta.

The Falcons have been lit up by RBs recently with injuries taking a toll, allowing Bucky Irving (170 total yards), Christian McCaffrey (RB6) and D'Andre Swift (RB5) to run wild. They also just traded away safety Jessie Bates this week. This sets up a potential big game with the Chiefs projected for 25.25 points as 3.5-point road favorites.

articles.title: New A.J. Brown, Rhamondre Stevenson Injury Updates Ahead of Patriots' Game vs. Lions in Germany
articles.summary: The New England Patriots have been riddled with injuries throughout the 2026 season, but two of their top offensive weapons may be available on Sunday, with running back Rhamondre Stevenson and wide receiver A.J. Brown both in contention to play, according to ESPN's Mike Reiss.
articles.body:
The New England Patriots have been riddled with injuries throughout the 2026 season, but two of their top offensive weapons may be available on Sunday, with running back Rhamondre Stevenson and wide receiver A.J. Brown both in contention to play, according to ESPN's Mike Reiss .

Stevenson suffered a knee injury during the team's loss to the Green Bay Packers last week. Early reports suggested that he could miss several weeks , but the running back has been "pushing to play."

Brown missed the past two games because of a knee issue, but he returned to practice this week. Vrabel felt "pretty good" about the wide receiver's status on Friday, per Reiss.

New England traded a 2028 first-round pick to acquire Brown from the Philadelphia Eagles in the offseason, and he was expected to serve as the top target for quarterback Drake Maye. So far, the results have been underwhelming.

Brown suffered an ankle injury in the regular-season opener and missed four games. He returned from the injured reserve in Week 6 and played against the New York Jets and Chicago Bears, but landed on the injury report with a knee issue after playing those two games in the span of four days.

The 29-year-old wide receiver has just nine receptions for 101 yards in three games this season.

Stevenson has arguably been New England's best offensive skill player this season. The sixth-year running back has 399 rushing yards and two touchdowns on 102 carries. He's also added 26 catches for 258 yards and two scores in the passing game. Stevenson leads the team with 657 yards from scrimmage.

New England can't afford to be without Stevenson, especially since running back TreVeyon Henderson was ruled out with an illness. Henderson has missed the past three games after being hospitalized with a medical emergency involving neurological symptoms, according to Mark Daniels of MassLive.

The Patriots have not lost back-to-back games under head coach Mike Vrabel, according to Reiss, but it won't be easy to keep that streak alive. New England will face the Detroit Lions on Sunday at the FC Bayern Stadium in Munich, Germany.

articles.title: Amon-Ra St. Brown Teases Germany Celebration vs. Patriots If He Scores 1st TD Since September
articles.summary: Detroit Lions star Amon-Ra St. Brown hopes to show off a German-themed touchdown celebration if he gets into the end zone during Sunday's game against the New England Patriots at Allianz Arena in Munich, Germany.
articles.body:
Detroit Lions star Amon-Ra St. Brown hopes to show off a German-themed touchdown celebration if he gets into the end zone during Sunday's game against the New England Patriots at Allianz Arena in Munich, Germany.

St. Brown, whose mother is from Germany, told reporters after Friday's practice he is working to figure out the proper celebration.

"I got to do something Germany related, with the culture, whether it's soccer," St. Brown said. "Anything German culture is what it's going to be. But exactly what I don't know yet. ... I don't have it planned yet. I got like two days to figure that out. I haven't been in the end zone in some weeks, so I feel like Germany would be a great time to touch the paint again."

Washington Commanders running back Craig Reynolds, who played with St. Brown in Detroit from 2021 to '25, told ESPN's Eric Woodyard the four-time Pro Bowler will regularly speak German when talking to his mom or brother:

"He speaks German to his mom all the time. Or he'll speak it to his brother if we're in public and they're trying to say something. But I don't like it because I don't know German. I feel like they're sneak dissing me when I'm around, so I don't like that s--t. "I've told him multiple times like, 'You can't be doing that when I'm around. Or you've got to tell me what you're saying or teach me what you're saying.' It's not fair for me to be in an elevator and you're talking to your brother in German while other people don't know what you're saying."

St. Brown holds dual citizenship between the United States and Germany. He also played for the German U19 football team in 2015 along with his brother, Osiris, that finished second at European Championships.

A touchdown on Sunday would also snap St. Brown's five-game drought. It's his longest streak without a touchdown since the 2022 season.

The Lions and Patriots will kickoff Sunday's NFL slate at 9:30 a.m. ET.

articles.title: Darian Mensah, Eagles GM Howie Roseman Meet in Viral Video at Miami Game After NFL Trade Deadline
articles.summary: Amid speculation about the Philadelphia Eagles potentially drafting a quarterback this year, general manager Howie Roseman fanned the flames.
articles.body:
Amid speculation about the Philadelphia Eagles potentially drafting a quarterback this year, general manager Howie Roseman fanned the flames.

Roseman made an appearance at Miami's matchup against Duke on Saturday and met up with quarterback Darian Mensah before the game.

Mensah is widely considered to be one of the top quarterbacks in this year's draft class, and it wouldn't be out of the realm of possibility for the Eagles to consider taking him if he's on the board.

articles.title: NFL Hall of Famer Fran Tarkenton has paid $51.89 million for a renovated five-bedroom Palm Beach mansion; the sellers had bought the property for $12.65 million in 2019 before overhauling its interiors
articles.summary: Former Minnesota Vikings quarterback Fran Tarkenton has bought a renovated five-bedroom mansion in Palm Beach, Florida, for a recorded $51.89 million,
articles.body: Former Minnesota Vikings quarterback Fran Tarkenton has bought a renovated five-bedroom mansion in Palm Beach, Florida, for a recorded $51.89 million, according to property records cited by Palm Beach Daily News. The 86-year-old Pro Football Hall of Famer purchased the Mediterranean-style residence at 1620 South Ocean Boulevard through the Tarkenton Revocable Trust. The sellers, Anthony and Lynda Lomangino, had acquired the property for $12.65 million in 2019 before undertaking an extensive renovation.The property is located on a stretch of South Ocean Boulevard known locally as Billionaires Row, a little over a mile south of US President Donald Trump's Mar-a-Lago Club. It sits on a corner lot measuring more than half an acre, across the road from the Atlantic Ocean, and comes with private beach access, according to its real estate listing. The two-storey Mediterranean-style home was built in 2006. Its sellers carried out a major overhaul, with the property described in the listing as having been rebuilt from the roof down. The renovation included a new roof, impact-resistant windows, updated landscaping, a generator and a new air-conditioning system.The interiors feature marble detailing, French wood-inlay flooring and pecky-cypress ceilings. The formal living room and a paneled library face the sea, while the second-floor primary bedroom suite also looks out towards the ocean. The suite includes a separate sitting room, two bathrooms and two closets. It also has a balcony with ocean views.The kitchen is fitted with a La Cornue stove and an island designed to seat 10 people. Other features include a card room, an elevator and a three-car garage. An open-air dining loggia with a fireplace overlooks a courtyard with a swimming pool and whirlpool spa. The property also has a newly built courtyard and landscaped outdoor spaces.The sales listing describes the house as offering more than 10,000 square feet of space. The property is spread across a lot of more than half an acre, with the ocean visible across South Ocean Boulevard. The mansion's location and private beach access were among the features highlighted in the marketing material.Tarkenton's agent, Jana Scarpa of Compass Florida, told Homes.com News that the former quarterback and his wife, Linda, had visited Palm Beach for years and were familiar with the area. She said she had a particular property in mind for them. Recalling their reaction when they entered the house, Scarpa said: "They walked in and said, 'Sold.'"Scarpa also represented the Lomanginos when they bought the property in 2019, making the latest transaction a return to a deal she had handled years earlier. According to Palm Beach Daily News, she said the sale brought the process "full circle" and that selling the property again was especially meaningful to her. She represented the buyers in the latest transaction, while Christian Angle of Christian Angle Real Estate was the listing broker.The mansion had been put on the market for $59 million, according to the listing broker's announcement. The recorded sale price of $51.89 million was therefore below the asking price. The difference between the Lomanginos' 2019 purchase price and the latest sale is substantial, although the renovation costs and other expenses associated with the property have not been publicly detailed. The gap between the two transaction prices should not be treated as the sellers' profit.For Tarkenton, the purchase comes decades after a career that made him one of the most recognisable quarterbacks of his generation. He began his NFL career with the Minnesota Vikings in 1961 and played for the franchise until 1966, before joining the New York Giants. He returned to Minnesota in 1972 and remained with the Vikings until retiring in 1978.Known for his ability to evade defenders and extend plays, Tarkenton helped lead the Vikings to three NFC championships. He was named the NFL's Most Valuable Player in 1975 and earned nine Pro Bowl selections during his career. At the time of his retirement, he held several major passing records, including career completions, passing yards and touchdown passes.Tarkenton was inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 1986. According to the Hall of Fame's records, he finished his career with 47,003 passing yards and 342 touchdown passes. After football, he worked in the computer-software industry, ran a business-consulting company and served as a commentator on *Monday Night Football* from 1979 to 1982.The Palm Beach purchase adds Tarkenton to the list of wealthy buyers drawn to the island's high-end property market. The Lomanginos, meanwhile, have also been active in the area's luxury real estate scene. Earlier in 2026, they paid a recorded $76.74 million for Villa Flora, a landmarked oceanfront mansion designed by architect Addison Mizner in 1923.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? images.caption: Kim Kardashian's $148 SKIMS advent calendar sparks a holiday shopping storm: Here's why
